title: Preregistration Record: Block I B2 Causal Maintenance Network - Theory of Everything Research Programme

pilot.use: Implementation validation and pilot-informed selection of disturbance regimes, edge threshold, rescue magnitude criteria, and bypass margins only. Pilot data are excluded from confirmatory evidence.

confirmatory_seeds.generation: NumPy default_rng (PCG64) initialised with 20261001; unique 9-digit integers were drawn and frozen before confirmatory execution.

architectures.C_feedforward: Internal C1->C2 and C1->C3 maintenance, with 40% source self-maintenance allocation and total budget 0.03.
architectures.D_reciprocal: Internal C1->C2->C3->C1 reciprocal maintenance, total budget 0.03.
architectures.E_bruteforce: Direct deficit-based internal repair with total budget 0.03 and no reciprocal maintenance graph; serious bypass/null.

analysis.experimental_unit: registered seed within architecture/condition; repeated time steps are nested observations, not independent replicates
analysis.uncertainty: Wilson 95% intervals for viability proportions; paired percentile bootstrap 95% intervals for continuous paired differences using 10000 resamples and analysis RNG seed 20261002; Kaplan-Meier-style right-censored failure-time summaries are descriptive.
analysis.primary_inference: Fixed preregistered thresholds and seed-consistency criteria; no primary null-hypothesis p-value testing.
analysis.multiplicity: Only C1 is preregistered for decisive node ablation, so no familywise correction is required for the primary edge test. Any additional node ablations are exploratory.

H1.1.claim: Active maintenance provides a selective advantage over passive stability when disturbances require continuing correction.
H1.1.retain: Low-disturbance passive path viability >=16/20; medium passive path viability lies between low and high passive viability; high-disturbance passive path viability <=4/20; at least 3 of 4 active architectures have high-disturbance path viability >=16/20; mean high-disturbance active-minus-passive path-viability advantage >=0.60.
H1.1.restrict: Active advantage is reproducible but the graded disturbance or architecture-breadth criteria are not all met.
H1.1.suspend: Passive path viability <16/20 under low disturbance, making the passive comparator too fragile for the intended graded-demand test.
H1.1.reject: Passive persistence matches active systems under high disturbance after matched degradation/disturbance controls.

H1.2.claim: Internally maintained systems retain greater operational viability than externally maintained systems after external support is withdrawn.
H1.2.retain: External terminal viability <=4/20; feed-forward, reciprocal, and brute-force internal architectures each >=16/20; at least 2 internal architectures exceed external mean terminal minimum-state by >=0.25.
H1.2.restrict: Internal advantage is reproducible but one or more magnitude/consistency thresholds are missed.
H1.2.reduce: External support withdrawal does not selectively disadvantage the externally maintained system or simpler persistence explains the same survival.
H1.2.reject: External and internal systems show equivalent autonomous persistence after support withdrawal.

H1.3.claim: Reciprocal maintenance topology predicts topology-specific propagation of targeted C1 failure.
H1.3.retain: Mean paired intact-minus-ablated reciprocal C2 effect > epsilon_w=0.25; at least 16/20 seeds have C2 deficit >=0.30 and C2 deficit exceeds C3 deficit by >=0.20; feed-forward absolute C2-versus-C3 deficit difference <=0.15 in at least 16/20 seeds.
H1.3.restrict: A reciprocal downstream effect is reproducible but topology selectivity/feed-forward discrimination misses one or more thresholds.
H1.3.reduce: Simpler feed-forward structure, raw deficit allocation, or brute-force repair reproduces the same propagation signature.
H1.3.reject: Reciprocal C1-to-C2 effect does not exceed epsilon_w or predicted propagation repeatedly fails.

H1.4.claim: Specific functional replacement rescues the predicted downstream deficit caused by C1 removal.
H1.4.retain: Specific rescue raises terminal C2 by >=0.30 on average versus no-rescue ablation and by >=0.30 in at least 16/20 seeds; specific rescue exceeds equal-budget irrelevant rescue in terminal C2 by >=0.30 on average and in >=16/20 seeds; irrelevant rescue improves C2 by <0.10 on average versus no-rescue ablation.
H1.4.restrict: Specific rescue is reproducibly beneficial but selectivity/magnitude thresholds are not all met.
H1.4.reject: Matched specific rescue fails systematically or irrelevant rescue restores C2 equivalently.

H1.5.scope: This first B2 preregistration fixes one three-component system boundary and one native simulation step resolution. No claim of boundary or timescale robustness will be made from this study.

H1.6.claim: Reciprocal organisation provides maintenance outcomes not reducible to passive stability, external support, or maintenance budget alone.
H1.6.retain_within_tested_class: Reciprocal architecture exceeds brute-force bypass by >0.10 in path viability or >0.10 in mean terminal minimum-state under high disturbance, and the bypass fails the ablation noninferiority criterion, while H1.3/H1.4 retain.
H1.6.restrict: Reciprocal advantage appears only under the registered perturbation context rather than ordinary viability.
H1.6.reduce: Brute-force bypass is noninferior to reciprocal maintenance: absolute high-disturbance path-viability difference <=0.10; mean terminal minimum-state difference <=0.10; and after C1 ablation, brute-force mean state of non-ablated C2/C3 is no more than 0.05 below reciprocal. A REDUCE verdict does not negate causal reality of a reciprocal edge if H1.3/H1.4 retain.
H1.6.reject: Serious matched alternatives reproduce all decisive outcomes and no selective causal contribution of the proposed internal organisation survives.

overall_interpretation.internal_maintenance: May receive RETAIN even if reciprocal-topology necessity receives REDUCE, provided H1.1, H1.2 and H1.4 demonstrate reproducible selective causal maintenance effects.
overall_interpretation.reciprocal_topology: Receives a separate verdict. Causal edge validation does not imply necessity.
overall_interpretation.scope_limit: Any positive result is limited to artificial functional/causal self-maintenance in this fixed three-component architecture family. It does not establish life, biological organisational closure, origin-of-life history, intelligence, consciousness, or universal TP1 necessity.
